SYS_1011.title: Cell overvoltage protection
SYS_1011.content: The battery management system shall disconnect the traction battery from the high-voltage circuit when the voltage of any cell exceeds 4.25 V for longer than 100 ms.
SYS_1011.rationale: Sustained overvoltage plates lithium on the anode and is a primary thermal-runaway initiator.

SYS_1012.title: Cell undervoltage protection
SYS_1012.content: The battery management system shall disconnect the traction battery from the high-voltage circuit when the voltage of any cell falls below 2.50 V for longer than 100 ms.
SYS_1012.rationale: Deep discharge dissolves the copper current collector and causes internal short circuits on the next charge.

SYS_1013.title: Pack overcurrent protection
SYS_1013.content: The battery management system shall disconnect the traction battery from the high-voltage circuit when the pack discharge current exceeds 400 A for longer than 50 ms.
SYS_1013.rationale: Sustained overcurrent exceeds the thermal rating of the cell tabs and the contactor weld limit.

SYS_1014.title: Cell overtemperature protection
SYS_1014.content: The battery management system shall disconnect the traction battery from the high-voltage circuit when the temperature of any cell exceeds 60 degC.
SYS_1014.rationale: Above 60 degC the separator begins to lose mechanical integrity.

SYS_1015.title: Contactor opening time
SYS_1015.content: The battery management system shall de-energise both high-voltage contactor channels within 10 ms of issuing a protective disconnect command.
SYS_1015.rationale: The reaction time budget for the vehicle-level safety goal allocates 10 ms to the contactor stage.

SYS_1016.title: Protective disconnect latching
SYS_1016.content: The battery management system shall keep the traction battery disconnected after a protective disconnect until the fault has been cleared by a qualified service procedure.
SYS_1016.rationale: An intermittent fault condition must never silently re-close the high-voltage circuit.

SYS_1021.title: State of charge accuracy
SYS_1021.content: The battery management system shall report the pack state of charge with an absolute error of no more than 3 percent across the full operating range.
SYS_1021.rationale: Range estimation and charge planning at vehicle level depend on this accuracy.

SYS_1022.title: State of health reporting
SYS_1022.content: The battery management system shall report the pack state of health with an absolute error of no more than 5 percent over the service life of the pack.
SYS_1022.rationale: Warranty assessment and residual value estimation rely on a trustworthy capacity-fade figure.

SYS_1023.title: Power limit prediction
SYS_1023.content: The battery management system shall report the maximum charge and discharge power available for the next 10 seconds.
SYS_1023.rationale: The drive inverter and the charger both need a forward-looking limit to avoid tripping protection.

SYS_1024.title: Low temperature charge accuracy
SYS_1024.content: The battery management system shall maintain the stated state of charge accuracy down to a pack temperature of -20 degC.
SYS_1024.rationale: Cold-climate markets report the largest range-estimation complaints.

SYS_1031.title: Active cooling activation
SYS_1031.content: The battery management system shall request active cooling when the highest cell temperature exceeds 40 degC.
SYS_1031.rationale: Sustained operation above 40 degC accelerates calendar ageing disproportionately.

SYS_1032.title: Preconditioning before fast charge
SYS_1032.content: The battery management system shall request pack heating when the lowest cell temperature is below 0 degC and a fast charge session has been requested.
SYS_1032.rationale: Fast charging below freezing causes lithium plating and permanent capacity loss.

SYS_1033.title: Cell temperature uniformity
SYS_1033.content: The battery management system shall keep the temperature difference between the hottest and coldest cell below 5 K during normal operation.
SYS_1033.rationale: Temperature spread drives divergent ageing and therefore pack-level capacity loss.

SYS_1041.title: Cell balancing window
SYS_1041.content: The battery management system shall equalise the cell voltages when the difference between the highest and lowest cell exceeds 50 mV.
SYS_1041.rationale: Cell divergence reduces the usable capacity of the whole pack to that of its weakest cell.

SYS_1042.title: Balancing during charging
SYS_1042.content: The battery management system shall continue cell balancing while the pack is being charged.
SYS_1042.rationale: The charge phase offers the longest uninterrupted window in which balancing is effective.

SYS_1051.title: Insulation resistance monitoring
SYS_1051.content: The battery management system shall continuously measure the insulation resistance between the high-voltage circuit and the vehicle chassis.
SYS_1051.rationale: Loss of isolation exposes the vehicle body to high voltage and is a direct electrocution hazard.

SYS_1052.title: Isolation fault indication
SYS_1052.content: The battery management system shall indicate an isolation fault to the driver and record it when the insulation resistance falls below 500 ohm per volt.
SYS_1052.rationale: The threshold is mandated for high-voltage vehicle circuits.

SYS_1061.title: Over-the-air firmware update
SYS_1061.content: The battery management system shall support over-the-air update of its firmware with the ability to roll back to the previously installed version.
SYS_1061.rationale: Field campaigns must not require a workshop visit for every software defect.

SYS_1062.title: Secure boot
SYS_1062.content: The battery management system shall verify the authenticity of its firmware before executing it.
SYS_1062.rationale: A forged firmware image would defeat every protection function in this specification.

SYS_1063.title: Diagnostic service interface
SYS_1063.content: The battery management system shall provide diagnostic services in accordance with ISO 14229 over the vehicle diagnostic bus.
SYS_1063.rationale: Workshop tooling across the vehicle programme is standardised on UDS.

SYS_1064.title: End-of-line current sensor calibration
SYS_1064.content: The battery management system shall support calibration of its current sensor offset during end-of-line production testing.
SYS_1064.rationale: Uncalibrated sensor offset is the dominant error term in coulomb counting.

SYS_1065.title: Safety event data recording
SYS_1065.content: The battery management system shall record the 30 seconds of pack measurements preceding any protective disconnect and retain them for later retrieval.
SYS_1065.rationale: Field failure analysis currently depends on reproducing the fault on a bench.
